hrec.reported_cause: Development face was blasted; it ignited the inflammable gas accumulated in the opposite gallery (burn injuries to blasting crewman posted as guard).
hrec.cause_status: Official DGMS enquiry finding ("Had ... could have been averted")
hrec.situation: While development face lying within 2.5m of an opposite gallery, was blasted in an underground coal mine, it ignited the inflammable gas accumulated therein the opposite gallery, inflicting serious burn injuries to a blasting crewman posted as guard, who died in the hospital after about forty two hours during treatment.
findings: the test for presence of inflammable gas in the joining gallery lying within 2.5m of the face of firing been made before charging and firing the shots as required under the provisions of Regulation 175(2) of the coal mines regulation 1957

the tests for inflammable gas been made in the area lying within 20m of the place of firing in each shift and a record thereof maintained in a bound paged book required to be kept maintained for the purpose as required under clause 3(c) of the permission of solid blasting granted vide this Directorate's letter no. NR-1/133 dated 27.01.2014 under the provision of Regulation 168(15), 173(a) & (c) and 175 of the Coal Mines Regulation 1957

the working places including the unused working temporarily stopped been inspected and examined for ventilation and presence of inflammable gases within two hours before commencement of work in a shift and at least in every four hours during which shift continues, as required under Regulation 113(3)(b) of the Coal Mines Regulation 1957

the gallery lying within 2.5m of the place of firing which was likely to be punctured, been inspected by a competent person for the presence of inflammable gas at least once in every seven days and a record thereof been maintained in a bound paged book required to be kept maintained for the purpose, as required under Regulation 143 of the Coal Mines Regulation 1957

the galleries not been extended beyond 4.5m from the nearest ventilation connection without coursing of current of air up to a point within 4.5m of the face by means of a fire resistant pipes, tubes, brattices or any other material so as to ensure that the velocity of air current within 4.5m of the discontinued face is not less than 30m per minute to produce ventilation adequate to dilute gases that are inflammable or noxious so as to render them harmless, as required under the provisions of the Regulations 130(1), 146 (1) and Regulation 136A of the Coal Mines Regulation 1957
hrec.statutes: Coal Mines Regulations 1957; DGMS permission condition
hrec.notes: Gas concentration not reported in source. Gas type given only as "inflammable gas" (methane not named).

hrec.ignition: Round of shots fired in adjoining face
hrec.reported_cause: Round of shots fired in one face without withdrawing person from other face; two faces had approached within 2.0m; flying coal fragments from blown-through shots hit a dresser.
hrec.cause_status: Official DGMS enquiry finding ("Had ... could have been averted")
hrec.situation: While two working faces in a development district had approached within 2.0 m of each other and a round of shots was fired in one of the said faces, without withdrawing person from the other, flying fragments of coal released due to blown through of shots from the other side of parting hit a dresser who was present in other face, inflicting injuries on head and eye of dresser to which he succumbed almost instantly.
findings: the person was withdrawn from other face approached within 2.0 m of the face, where a round of shots was fired by the Shotfirer as required under the provision of the Regulation 170(3) of the Coal Mines Regulations,1957

the Overman and Shotfirer been vigilant and taken necessary steps to withdraw person from other face approached within 2.0 m of the face, where a round of shots was fired by the shotfirer, as required under the provision of the Regulation 170(3) of the Coal Mines Regulations,1957 read with Tech. circular no.16 of 1982 and Regulation 43(1) of the Coal Mines Regulations,1957

the Mining Sirdar been placed in the development district by the Asst. Manager to ensure that person was withdrawn from other face approached within 2.0 m of the face, where a round of shots was fired by the Shotfirer as required under the provision of the Regulation 170(3) of the Coal Mines Regulations,1957 read with Tech. circular no.1 of 1977 & circular No.4 of 1996 and Regulation 42(1) of the Coal Mines Regulations,1957

the card system for blasting been followed strictly in the development district as required under Regulation 170(3) of the Coal Mines Regulations,1957 read with Tech. circular no.4 of 1996 and Regulation 41(9) of the Coal Mines Regulations,1957

hrec.reported_cause: During deep hole blasting in overburden benches, flying fragments travelled 280m and hit a blasting helper (guard).
hrec.cause_status: Official DGMS enquiry finding ("Had ... could have been averted")
hrec.situation: While deep hole blasting was conducted in overburden benches of an opencast coal mine, flying fragments travelled by a distance of 280m to hit one of the blasting helpers(guard) present there who died on the spot soon after.
findings: the blasting helper (guard) taken proper shelter himself after evacuation of persons from danger zone as required under Reg.170(1A)(b), Reg.45(b) and Reg.43(d) of the CMR,1957.
the burden from free face kept as per blast design.
there been adequate blasting shelters for taking shelter during blasting operation as required under Reg. 170(2) of CMR,1957.

hrec.reported_cause: Rotating drill bit hit a misfire shot of earlier blasting which exploded; a crater of about 1.2x1.2m "0.5 size" (as printed) formed; fly-off rock and ejected iron pieces of the drill machine hit a contractual worker.
hrec.cause_status: Official DGMS enquiry finding ("Had ... could have been averted")
hrec.situation: While drilling was being carried out by deploying a drill on a overburden bench in night shift in an opencast coal mine the rotating drill bit hit to a misfire shot of earlier blasting, which exploded, a crater of about 1.2x1.2m 0.5 size was formed at the drilling place, the fly off rocks & ejected iron pieces of drill machine hit to a contractual worker engaged for demarcation of position of shot holes and cleaning of drill cutting, thus inflicting serious bodily injuries to which be succumbed on way to hospital.
findings: the misfires was detected & dealt with properly before drilling new hole, as required under regulation 204 also read with reg. 239 of the CMR, 2017 and para 6.0 of the code of practice for blasting framed by the manger
hrec.statutes: Coal Mines Regulations 2017; SOP / code of practice / SMP
hrec.notes: Crater dimension printed as "1.2x1.2m 0.5 size" - retained verbatim.

hrec.reported_cause: While reversing, a dozer rolled over an oxygen cylinder kept on the surface near a coal heap, causing an explosion that burned a mechanical fitter in the vicinity.
hrec.cause_status: Official DGMS enquiry finding ("Had ... could have been averted")
hrec.situation: While reversing, a dozer rolled over an oxygen cylinder kept on the surface near coal heap and caused explosion inflicting serious burn injuries to in fitter the vicinity, to which he succumbed after 24 hours during treatment in hospital.
findings: the operator been more vigilant and been ensured that the place for movement of dozer should be free from any object thus negligently or wilfully did thing likely to endanger life or, negligently or wilfully omitted to do thing necessary for the safety of the persons employed therein in contravention of the provision of Regulation 239 of coal Mines Regulation 2017.

oxygen cylinders when not in use been kept in trolley or inside fenced area where there is no movement of HEMM as to obviate any risk of fire, bursting or explosion in contraventions of the provision of Regulation 210(1) of Coal Mines Regulation 2017.
hrec.notes: Classified by the source under Dust/Gas/Other Combustible Material (0779), not under Explosives.

hrec.reported_cause: A tipper entered the danger zone while a coal bench was blasted and was overturned by the effect of blasting.
hrec.cause_status: Official DGMS enquiry finding ("Had ... could have been averted")
hrec.situation: While a coal bench of an opencast mine was blasted, a tipper engaged in transportation of coal entered within the danger zone at that instant and was overturned due to effect of blasting inflicting serious bodily injuries to the tipper operator who died on the way to the hospital.
findings: the tipper not been allowed to enter within a radius of 500m from the place of blasting hereinafter referred to as the danger zone as required under Regulation 196(2)(b) of the Coal Mines Regulations, 2017 read with Reg. 194 of the Coal Mines Regulations, 2017 read with the Gazette of India Notification No. G.S.R. 985(E), Condition 25.0, dated, 1st October, 2018

hrec.ignition: Lower patch initiated before withdrawal of persons (miscommunication)
hrec.reported_cause: While charging deep holes with SME explosive and detonating cord on an upper overburden bench, the lower patch (already charged and interconnected by detonating cord) was initiated without withdrawal of persons from the upper patch (miscommunication), causing explosion in both charged patches.
hrec.cause_status: Official DGMS enquiry finding ("Had ... could have been averted")
hrec.situation: While charging of deep holes with SME explosive and Detonating cord was being carried out in an overburden bench immediately above the other overburden bench already charged with SME Explosive and interconnected with the detonating cord in view of blasting the two patches simultaneously with initiation at lower patch in an opencast coal mine, the lower patch was initiated for blasting without ensuring for withdrawal of persons at upper OB patch due to some miscommunication causing the explosion in both the charged patches, in which one person succumbed on the spot and three persons including the Overman got serious injuries and another two persons got reportable injuries at the upper patch.
findings: the upper patch been not connected with lower patch by detonating cord and also the detonator & blasting cable not connected to shot-firing apparatus in lower patch, before withdrawal of persons working at upper patch, thus negligently not endangering the life of persons, as required under Reg. 195(8)(c)&(d) of the CMR, 2017
the warning Siren been not blown before the withdrawal of persons at upper patch being charged, to avoid the miscommunication, as required under Reg. 196(2)(b) of the CMR, 2017

the key of the exploder been retained in possession of Overman at lower patch throughout the charging and blasting activities, thus negligently not endangering the lfe of persons working at upper patch, as required under Reg. 195(7)(c) of the CMR, 2017
hrec.notes: Statement 6.3 shows 3 injured in this fatal accident (serious); the 2 reportable injuries appear only in the narrative. Minor/reportable injuries: 2 reportable injuries (narrative)

hrec.reported_cause: While seven persons charged explosive into large-diameter holes drilled in boulders (about 2.0m x 3.0m x 3.0m) for secondary blasting, the explosive column poured in the hole exploded: 3 killed on the spot, 1 died on the way to hospital, 3 seriously injured.
hrec.cause_status: Official DGMS enquiry finding ("Had ... could have been averted")
hrec.situation: While a group of seven persons were charging explosive in large diameter holes, drilled in big boulders, measuring about 2.0m x 3.0m x 3.0m, for secondary blasting in an opencast coal mine, suddenly the explosive column, poured in hole, exploded inflicting fatal injuries to three of them on the spot, one person succumbed to his injuries on the way to hospital and rest three persons were seriously injured.
findings: the hazards associated with charging of large diameter holes into boulders, lying at a place not convenient for charging, been identified, its risk been assessed & eliminated/minimized/controlled at source and the work been done as required under the documented SMP of the mine, prepared in accordance with Regulation 104(1), Regulation 104(2) and Regulation 104(3) of the Coal Mines Regulation, 2017

the SOP been framed as part of SMP, in accordance with the identified hazards and assessed risk for charging SME explosive, as required under Regulation 104(5)(e) and implemented under Regulation 104(8) of the Coal Mines Regulation, 2017

the persons, employed in handling and use of explosive including SME explosive, been imparted training for that purpose as required under Rule 13 of the Mines Vocational Training Rules, 1966 as detailed in 6th schedule

the unsafe practice of drilling large dia. holes in boulders for secondary blasting and charging those hole with SME explosive not been done, thereby negligently and wilfully endangering lives of persons, employed in mines as required under Regulation 239 of the Coal Mines Regulation, 2017

it been ensured that the large diameter hole in boulders was charged with SME explosive from easily reachable place, thereby not negligently and wilfully endangering lives of persons employed in mines as required under Regulation 239 of the Coal Mines Regulation, 2017.
hrec.statutes: Coal Mines Regulations 2017; Mines Vocational Training Rules 1966; SOP / code of practice / SMP
hrec.notes: Same event appears in: Statement 7.8 narrative (p.226), Major Accident box (p.198) and Chapter 10 list sl.283 (p.306). Counted once.

hrec.ignition: UDM drill rod holed into misfired shot
hrec.reported_cause: Drill rod of a Universal Drilling Machine accidentally holed into a misfired shot of the previous shift, which exploded; helper hit by projectiles.
hrec.cause_status: Official DGMS enquiry finding ("Had ... could have been averted")
hrec.situation: While a UDM(Universal Drilling Machine) operator was drilling holes with UDM at the floor near a split face of depillaring panel in an underground mine, the drill rod of the UDM accidently holed into a misfired shot of previous shift causing it to explode, in which an UDM helper who was present near the face was hit by the projectiles of the explosion receiving multiple injuries, to which he succumbed on the way to hospital.
findings: a careful examination been made at the place after firing of shots before any other person was allowed to enter the place, as required under Regulation 49(f) read with Regulation 203(1) of the CMR 2017
the presence of misfired hole been reported to the succeeding shift by the shot-firer by recording in shot-firer's report book, as required under Regulation 206(2) of the CMR 2017

the working place been examined carefully and made safe and instructions to observe any special precaution been given to persons before allowing them to work, as required under Regulations 48(1) read with Regulations 48(2)(c) and 129(5) of the CMR 2017
an overman been deployed to hold charge of P-18 panel in each working shift for performing duties under these regulations, as required under Regulation 33(1) of the CMR 2017
hrec.notes: Checked against narrative and Statement x.3 counts.

hrec.reported_cause: Drill bit came in contact with the explosive charge of a misfire shot hole and blasted: 1 killed, 3 seriously injured; shotfirer escaped unhurt.
hrec.cause_status: Official DGMS enquiry finding ("Had ... could have been averted")
hrec.situation: While a crew of five persons engaged in drilling operation at a split gallery of an underground coal mine, suddenly the drill bit came in contact with explosive charge of a shot hole (misfire) and got blasted; inflicting fatal injuries to one of the crew member and serious injuries to the other three of them; while the shot firer escaped unhurt.
findings: the split gallery been examined and declared safe in all aspects including misfire before engaging drilling crew as required under the provisions of Regulation 203, 204, & 129(5) of Coal Mines Regulations, 2017
the code of practice for drilling and blasting and dealing with misfire shots been followed as required under the provisions of Regulation 110 and 204 of Coal Mines Regulations, 2017
hrec.statutes: Coal Mines Regulations 2017; SOP / code of practice / SMP
hrec.notes: Checked against narrative and Statement x.3 counts.

hrec.reported_cause: Blasting projectiles travelled and hit the cabin of an explosive van parked about 170m away, injuring the person sitting in it (door partially open).
hrec.cause_status: Official DGMS enquiry finding ("Had ... could have been averted")
hrec.situation: While a person was sitting in the cabin of explosive van by keeping the left door partially opened which was parked on haul road in front of blasting face and at about 170m away from place of blasting in an opencast coal mine, blasting projectiles travelled and hit the van cabin, inflicting serious injuries to him and to which he succumbed eight days later in hospital.
findings: the person not been negligently sat in the cabin of explosive van by keeping the door partially opened, which was parked in the vicinity of blasting, without taking proper shelter, by endangering his life in contravention of the Regulation 239 of the Coal Mines Regulations, 2017

the shot firer not been fired the shots without ensuring the taking of proper shelter by persons in the vicinity and within the danger zone of blasting in contravention of the Regulation 196(2)(a) &(b) of the Coal Mines Regulations, 2017

the blasting operation been stopped when the person found within the vicinity and danger zone of blasting by implementing the control measures defined in Safety Management Plan prepared by mine management vide No. CCL/B&K/BKO/Project officer/2013-14, dated 06.01.20214, which was reviewed vide No. PO/Bokaro Colliery/2021/2021-22/490, dated 24.04.2021, as required under Regulation 104 (3) of the Coal Mines Regulations, 2017.

the shot holes been effectively muffled to prevent blasting projectiles travel not more than 10.0m away from the place blasting as required by condition no. 5.5 of the permission granted vide this Directorate's letter no. KR/91, dated 29.01.2007 under Regulation 196(3) of the Coal Mines Regulations, 2017 (Reg. 170 (1A) & (1B) of the erstwhile Coal Mines Regulations, 1957)

the blasting not been done in broken and crushed overburden face in contravention with condition no. 5.7 of the permission granted vide this Directorate's letter no. KR/91, dated 29.01.2007 under Regulation 196(3) of the Coal Mines Regulations, 2017 (Reg. 170 (1A) & (18) of the erstwhile Coal Mines Regulations, 1957)
hrec.statutes: Coal Mines Regulations 1957; Coal Mines Regulations 2017; DGMS permission condition; SOP / code of practice / SMP
hrec.notes: Checked against narrative and Statement x.3 counts.

hrec.reported_cause: While a gang of 13 contractual workers loaded blasted stone adjacent to a charged round, some holes exploded prematurely due to a local lightning strike; fly rock killed 1 at once, 6 seriously injured (2 later died), 6 minor injuries.
hrec.cause_status: Official DGMS enquiry finding ("Had ... could have been averted")
hrec.situation: While loading of blasted stone by a gang of 13 contractual workers was in progress adjacent to a round of charged & stemmed shot-holes in a stone quarry, some of the charged holes exploded prematurely due to local strike of lightening, and the resulting fly rock inflicted fatal injuries to one person, serious bodily injuries to 6 persons and minor injuries to remaining 6 persons. Two of the seriously injured persons succumbed to their injuries whilst undergoing treatment at the hospital.
findings: All persons in the vicinity (other than the blaster and his assistants) been removed and allowed to take proper shelter before shot-holes were charged and stemmed, as required by the provisions of Regulation 164(1) of the Metalliferous Mines Regulations 1961, read with DGMS circular No. Tech. 7 of 2001

Detonators having adequate length of properly insulated leads ( commensureate with the depth of shot-holes) been used so that all connections in the round of shot-holes were properly made as required by the provisions of Regulation 163(4)(a) of the Metalliferous Mines Regulations 1961

During approach of a storm, all naked and exposed wires been coiled up and covered so as to prevent the charged holes from exploading prematurely by a local strike of the lightning, thus not negligently endangering life and safety of persons employed in the mine as required by the provisions of Regulation 181 of the Metalliferous Mines Regulations, 1961, read with Clause 8.2 of DGMS circular No. 36 of 1972, and DGMS circular no. Tech. 10 of 1995.
hrec.notes: Serious injured = 4 surviving of 6 seriously injured (2 died); consistent with Statement 3.2 (Stone, other explosive accidents: INJ 5 across 2 accidents incl. NC-03 = 1).

hrec.reported_cause: While shot holes were being charged, lightning struck and caused premature blasting: 2 killed, 1 seriously injured.
hrec.cause_status: Official DGMS enquiry finding ("Had ... could have been averted")
hrec.situation: While shot holes were being charged in an opencast stone quarry, suddenly electric storm started and lightning struck and caused premature blasting of charged shot holes inflicting fatal injuries to two persons and serious bodily injury to one person.
findings: during approach of an electric storm, all naked and exposed lead wires of detonators been coiled up in the mouth of shot holes or covered up by non conduction material, so as to prevent premature explosion of the charged by strike of lightning, thus not negligently endangering the life and safety of persons employed in the mine as required under the Regulation 181 of the Metalliferous Mines Regulations, 1961 read with DGMS (Technical) circular no. 1 of 1995
a manager possessing qualification as prescribed in the Regulation 34 of the Metalliferous Mines Regulations 1961 was kept in charge of the mine.

prepartion of charges, charging and stemming of holes in the mine was done by persons holding Manager's , foreman's Mate's or blaster's certificate as required under the Regulations 160(2) of the Metalliferous Mines Regulations 1961.
hrec.notes: Checked against narrative and Statement x.2 mineral/place counts.

hrec.reported_cause: Six 32mm shot holes charged with gun powder fired electrically by an unqualified supervisor; fly rock hit two workmen drilling 10m away.
hrec.cause_status: Official DGMS enquiry finding ("Had ... could have been averted")
hrec.situation: While six shot holes of 32mm in diameter were charged with gun powder and fired electrically by unqualified supervisor in a granite stone quarry, few fly rock projectiles hit two workmen engaged in drilling at a distance of 10m inflicting serious bodily injuries to both of them to which they succumbed on way to hospital.
findings: before a shot is charged, stemmed and fired ensured that all persons have taken proper shelter as required under the provisions of Regulation 164(1) of the Metalliferous Mines Regulations, 1961, a duly qualified blaster been appointed in the mine to perform the duties of blaster as required under the provision of Regulation 39(1) read with Regulation 160 of the Metalliferous Mines Regulation, 1961 and a duly qualified manager been appointed for overall management, control, supervision and direction of the mine as required under provisions of Section 18(4), Section 17 of the Mines Act, 1952 read with Regulation 34(1) of the Metalliferous Mines Regulations, 1961
hrec.notes: Checked against narrative and Statement x.2 mineral/place counts.

hrec.reported_cause: Charged holes blasted due to lightning during a thunderstorm; person returning from the bench hit by projectiles.
hrec.cause_status: Official DGMS enquiry finding ("Had ... could have been averted")
hrec.situation: While a person was returning from the working bench of an open-cast mine where drill holes were charged with explosives, it started raining with thunder storms and lighting due to which some of the charged holes got blasted due to lighting as a result of which he was fatally injured by the blasting projecties.
findings: a duly qualified manager been appointed and mine workings been placed under the charge of a mining mate as required under the provisions of 116(1) of the Metalliferous Mines Regulations,1961. all the persons other than blaster and his assistants in the vicinity been taken proper shelter before charging the drill holes and all exposed detonator lead wires are coiled up and placed in the mouth of the holes or kept covered by something other than a metal plate during lighting as required under the provisions of 164(1) and 106(2)(b) of the Metalliferous Mines Regulation,1961 read with DG's Technical Circular No.1 of 1995
hrec.notes: Checked against narrative and Statement x.2 mineral/place counts.

hrec.ignition: Not reported (explosive/detonating cord exploded during simultaneous drilling and charging)
hrec.reported_cause: Three persons drilling and charging a shot hole simultaneously; explosive/detonating cord exploded; all three died.
hrec.cause_status: Official DGMS enquiry finding ("Had ... could have been averted")
hrec.situation: While three persons were drilling and charging shot hole simultaneously on the bench of the opencast mine, suddenly the explosive/detonating cord exploded, causing serious injury to all, later to which they succumbed.
findings: The working of the mine been placed, under the supervision of a duly qualified person appointed as manager, thus not negligently endangering the life and safety of the work persons employed in the mine, as required under the provisions of Sec.18(4) of the Mines Act,1952 read with read with Reg.34(1) of the Metalliferous Mines Regulations,1961, The charging of holes been carried out by or under the personal supervision of a competent person/blaster, thus not negligently endangering the life and safety of the work persons employed in the mine, as required under the provisions of Regulation 160(1) of the Metalliferous Mines Regulations,1961. The working in the mine not being carried out in contravention of prohibitory order under section 22(3) of the Mines Act,1952, issued by this Directorate, thus not negligently endangering the life and safety of the work persons employed in the mine, as required under the provisions of Sec.18(4) of the Mines Act,1952. The explosive being used at the mine, been provided by the Owner,as required under the provisions of Sec.18(4) of the Mines Act,1952 read with Regulation 153 of the Metalliferous Mines Regulations,1961.
hrec.notes: Mine was working in contravention of a DGMS prohibitory order.

hrec.reported_cause: Four persons stemming and connecting shot holes; induced charge from lightning caused premature blasting; all four injured, two died after 1.5 and 2.75 hours.
hrec.cause_status: Narrative cause only (no findings printed)
hrec.situation: While four persons were stemming and making connection of shot holes in an opencast stone mine, the induced charge from sudden lighting resulted premature blasting of the charged shot holes, inflicting serious bodily injuries to all of them but two of them succumbed to their injuries at a hospital after 1 1/2 hours and 2 3/4 hours of the accident.
hrec.notes: Serious injured 2 = Statement 4.2 (Stone, other explosive accidents INJ 2).

hrec.ignition: Blasting circuit tested with a multimeter connected to detonator
hrec.reported_cause: While a blaster helper tested a blasting circuit with a multimeter, fifteen charged holes initiated; 1 trapped among boulders and died, 3 minor injuries.
hrec.cause_status: Official DGMS enquiry finding ("Had ... could have been averted")
hrec.situation: While a blaster helper was testing blasting circuit with a Multimeter after connecting to a detonator with detonating cord at the top bench of an Opencast workings, fifteen charged holes got initiated and blasted, inflicting injuries to four persons out of which one person got trapped among the blasted boulders and died on the spot and remaining three escaped with minor injuries.
findings: a duly qualified Manager been appointed for overall management, control, supervision and direction of the mine as required under Regulation 34 read with Section 17(1) of the Mines Act, 1952
a duly qualified blaster been appointed to carry out blasting operations as required under Regulation 160(2) of the Metalliferous Mines Regulations,1961
hrec.notes: Checked against narrative and Statement x.2 mineral/place counts.

hrec.xcat: Outside taxonomy: Hydrocarbon/vapour explosion in vessel
hrec.reported_cause: While three contract workers fixed a vent pipe on the roof of a wash tank at an Effluent Treatment Plant, a powerful explosion occurred in the tank; one thrown about 13m to the ground and died, two seriously injured.
hrec.cause_status: Narrative cause only (no findings printed)
hrec.situation: While three contractual persons were engaged in fixing of vent pipe on the roof top of a wash tank at new Effluent Treatment Plant (ETP) of Demalgoan-Lakhmani Production Oil Mine, Assam ONGC, there was a powerful explosion in the tank to which a person got thrown away on ground from a height of about 13 meter sustaining serious bodily injuries to which he succumbed at a hospital and two other persons got stuck to railing of the tank and survived with serious bodily injuries.
hrec.notes: Hot work not stated; category "vessel explosion" used because ignition source is not reported.

hrec.ignition: Jack-hammer drill rod penetrated unknown misfired hole
hrec.reported_cause: Drill rod penetrated an unknown misfire charge hole which exploded; 1 died after one hour, 1 seriously injured.
hrec.cause_status: Official DGMS enquiry finding ("Had ... could have been averted")
hrec.situation: While two persons were drilling holes with jack-hammer on the bench of an opencast stone quarry for blasting, the drill rod penetrated into unknown misfire charge hole, which lead to explosion, causing serious bodily injury to both of them. One of them was declared brought dead by the doctors at the hospital after one hour and other person was seriously injured on his left eye, nose and left side of abdomen.
findings: Manager, Foreman, Mining Mate & Blaster were appointed as required under the provisions of the Regulation 34, Regulation 37 and Regulation 39

Drilling and blasting operations were under personal supervision of a duly qualified Blaster for preparation of charges, charging and stemming of holes & firing as required under the provisions of Regulation 160
the misfire was clearly demarcated and had been dealt properly as per the provisions laid down under Regulation 167 of the Metalliferous Mines Regulations, 1961
hrec.notes: Checked against narrative and Statement x.2 mineral/place counts.

hrec.ignition: Jack-hammer drill rod encountered old charged hole
hrec.reported_cause: While drilling a granite block for slicing, the drill rod encountered an old charged hole which exploded; 1 died later in hospital.
hrec.cause_status: Official DGMS enquiry finding ("Had ... could have been averted")
hrec.situation: While two persons were drilling into a Granite block for slicing at the bed of a granite quarry by jack hammer drill the drill rod encountered an old charged hole and exploded due to which both the persons fell down inflicting serious bodily injuries to which one of them succumbed to death later in hospital.
findings: it been ensured that the granite block was throughly cleaned or washed down with water and carefully examined for the presence of misfires or sockets before commencement of drilling on it as required under Regulatioon 168 of the Metalliferous Mines Regulations, 1961

a duly qualified manager been appointed to have overall management, control, supervision and direction of the mine as required under Seciton 17 of the Mines act, 1952 read with the Regulation 34(1) of the Metalliferous Mines Regulation, 1961

effective supervision of the mine workings been provided by appointing a Foreman/Mining Mate as required under Regulation 37(1)(a)/39 read with Regulation 116 of the Metalliferous Mines Regulations, 1961
the persons employed in the mine been provided basic training as required under Rule 6 of the Mines Vocational Training Rules, 1966.
hrec.regulations: Reg 168; Reg 34(1); Reg 37(1)(a); Reg 116; Sec 17; Rule 6
hrec.statutes: Metalliferous Mines Regulations 1961; Mines Act 1952; Mines Vocational Training Rules 1966
hrec.notes: Checked against narrative and Statement x.2 mineral/place counts.

hrec.ignition: Mobile phone in possession while extending electric detonator lead wires
hrec.reported_cause: While a blasting helper extended lead wires of instantaneous electric detonators with a mobile phone in his possession, the detonator initiated the charge; projectiles killed him.
hrec.cause_status: Official DGMS enquiry finding ("Had ... could have been averted")
hrec.situation: While a blasting helper was extending the lead wires of instantaneous electric detonators connected to the detonating cord with mobile phone in his possession in an opencast working of a dimensional stone quarry, the detonator got initiated and detonated the explosive charge and subsequent resultant blast; the blasting projectiles of stone pieces have caused grievous injuries to the helper and died while being taken to hospital.
findings: the persons engaged in use of explosive been ensured that he don't possess any apparatus of kind capable of producing light, flame or spark or could initiate the explosive charge as required of him under the provisions of Reg. 170 read with condition no. 10.7 of permission vide letter No. HR-2/SCZ/106(2)(b)/30(18)/2018/319 Dated 18.01.2018 granted under Regulation 106(2)(b) of Metalliferous Mines Regulation 1961
the blaster himself been coupled up the cable to the detonating leads with due safety as required under the provisions 163(3)(c)(d)&(f), of Metalliferous Mines Regulation 1961

the person been strictly adhere to the provisions of the act and of the Regulations and orders there under and any order issued by official with a view to safety under Reg 41 of Metalliferous Mines Regulation 1961
the foreman ensured that the subordinate officials and competent persons in his district carry out their duties in proper manner as required under Reg 45(2)(a) of Metalliferous Mines Regulation 1961

the manager ensured that all operations carried on in connection with the mine are conducted in accordance with the provisions of this Act and of Regulations Bye- Laws orders made there under as required under section 18(4) of the Mines Act, 1952.
hrec.statutes: Metalliferous Mines Regulations 1961; Mines Act 1952; DGMS permission condition
hrec.notes: Narrative names the victim as "Blaster" in header and "blasting helper" in text.

hrec.reported_cause: 22 holes charged with 500gm explosive each, connected with instantaneous electric detonators, went off prematurely due to lightning; an outsider walking on the haul road was buried under blasted muck.
hrec.cause_status: Official DGMS enquiry finding ("Had ... could have been averted")
hrec.situation: While two outsiders were walking on a haul road of a mine, 22 numbers of holes charged with 500gm of explosive in each hole and connected with instantaneous electric detonators went off prematurely due to sudden strike of lightening. One of the outsiders was burried under the blasted muck resulting into serious bodily injury to which he succumbed on the spot whereas the other one escaped with minor injuries.
findings: it been ensured that all persons other than the assistant of the blaster have taken proper shelter and all of the persons within a radius of 300m been warned & withdrawn out from the mine with blowing of siren and electriccally exposed holes charged with explosive and connected with instantaneous electric detonators been covered with soil or any insulating material other than metal plate or conneciton of leads of instantaneous electric detonators of each hole been coiled and placed in the mouth of the holes as required under Regulation 164(1) & (1-A)(b) of te Metalliferous Mines Regulations, 1961 & DGMS Tech. Circular No. 1/1995 read with Section 18 of the Mines Act, 1952

the explosive been received, used and returned with signature of authorized person or official appointed by the owner of the mine and record regarding same being maintained properly as required under Regulations 156(3), 160 & 169(b) of the Metalliferous Mines Regulations, 1961 read with Section 18 of the Mines Act, 1952
hrec.statutes: Metalliferous Mines Regulations 1961; Mines Act 1952; DGMS circular
hrec.notes: Victim was an outsider. Statement 6.2 gives 1 seriously injured across NC-12 and NC-13 combined; not attributable, so left blank here.

hrec.reported_cause: Blaster and helper connecting lead wires of charged holes for secondary blasting; lightning caused accidental blast killing both.
hrec.cause_status: Official DGMS enquiry finding ("Had ... could have been averted")
hrec.situation: While a Blaster alongwith his helper was connecting lead wires of charged holes for secondary blasting in a road metal stone quarry due to lightning accidental blast occurred inflicting fatal injuries to both of them.
findings: the handling of detonators been discontinued during the approach of lightning storm as required under the provisions of the condition No. 10.3 of the permission granted under Regulation 106(2)(b) of Metalliferous Mines Regulations, 1961 vide letter No. HR-2/SCZ/106(2)(b)/98(16)/2016/2269 dated 19.07.2016 read with Regulation 181 of Metalliferous Mines Regulations, 1961.
hrec.statutes: Metalliferous Mines Regulations 1961; DGMS permission condition
hrec.notes: Checked against narrative and Statement x.2 mineral/place counts.

hrec.reported_cause: Misfired explosive cartridges in shot holes on top of the bench were initiated by lightning; projectiles killed two drillers at the bottom of the bench.
hrec.cause_status: Official DGMS enquiry finding ("Had ... could have been averted")
hrec.situation: While two drillers were at bottom of the bench of opencast stone quarry, the misfired explosive cartridges present in shot holes on the top of the bench, got initiated by lightning and projectiles of the blasting hit the said drillers inflicting serious bodily injuries to which both of them succumbed on the spot.
findings: a duly qualified manager been appointed for overall management, control, supervision, and direction of the mine during operation of the blasting as required under Regulation 34 of the Metalliferous Mines Regulations, 1961, read with section 17 of the Mines Act, 1952
Foreman been appointed in the mine to hold charge of the mine during blasting operation as required under Regulation 37 of the Metalliferous Mines Regulations, 1961
Mining Mate been appointed and workings been placed under the charge of mining mate as required under Regulation 39 read with Regulation 116 of the Metalliferous Mines Regulations, 1961

a duly qualified blaster been appointed for preparation of charges, charging and stemming of holes by him or under his personnel supervision and firing shots by himself as required under Regulation 39 read with Regulation 160 of the Metalliferous Mines Regulations, 1961
hrec.regulations: Reg 34; Reg 37; Reg 39; Reg 116; Reg 160; Sec 17
hrec.notes: See NC-12 note on unattributable serious injury.

hrec.xcat: Outside taxonomy: Hydrocarbon/vapour explosion in vessel
hrec.ignition: Gas cutting flame travelled through pipeline into tank
hrec.reported_cause: Gas cutting on a foam pourer pipeline connected to an oil storage tank; flame travelled through the pipeline and ignited hydrocarbon gases in the tank causing explosion; worker on the tank roof thrown 30m.
hrec.cause_status: Official DGMS enquiry finding ("Had ... could have been averted")
hrec.situation: While a gas cutting operation was being carried out by a welder on a foam pourer pipe line connected to a oil storage tank under maintenance filled with combustible hydrocarbon mixture, the flame travelled through pipeline and ignited hydrocarbon gases mixture inside the oil storage tank and caused explosion, resulting into severe burn injuries to an another workman who was standing over the roof of same tank holding the foam pourer pipe line and with impact of explosion he was thrown in air to a distance of 30m away, received serious bodily injuries to which he succumbed short while later.
findings: the positive isolation of storage tank been carried out using blind plates at storage tank Inlet, and 8 plunger valve meant for purpose of controlling flow of hydrocarbon to manifold been kept closed, thus preventing entry of hydrocarbon gas from system into oil storage tank as required under the provisions of Regulation 98(5)(t) of the Oil Mines Regulations, 2017 read with Oil Industry Safety Directorate (OISD) STD 105

hydrocarbons entrapped inside the storage tank been safely discharged before carrying out gas cutting operations on foam pipe lines and measurement of hydrocarbon gases to ensure absence of flammable gases inside the tank been ensured before commencing of job of cutting foam pipe line as required under the provisions of Regulation 98(4) & Regulation 98(5)(a) of the Oil Mines Regulations, 2017 read with Oil Industry Safety Directorate (OISD) STD 105 read with clause 14.2.1 of Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) document/Manual dated 24.12.2014

the vapour seal been provided & kept maintained to prevent entry of hydrocarbon from storage tank to foam pourer line and also the foam pourer line been completely disconnected, positively isolated before carrying out its gas cutting operations as required under the provisions of Regulation 100(5)(a), Regulation 109(1) & Regulation 98(5)(f) of the Oil Mines Regulations, 2017 read with Oil Industr Industry Safety Directorate (OISD) STD 105

the vents, breather valve, pressure relief safety valve over the oil storage tank and gate valve to oil storage tank been examined, tested and kept maintained to ensure their safe working order as required under the provisions of Regulation 109(1) of the Oil Mines Regulations, 2017 read with 8.1.2 of Oil Industry Safety Directorate (OISD) STD 132

authorized welder been appointed for hot work and persons engaged in gas cutting operations in Zone 1 hazardous area been provided adequate training in safety and been made aware of risks associated with hot work by the person issuing the hot work permit before the commencement of job, thus negligently not endangering their life as required under provisions of Regulation 98(1)&(3) and Regulation 133 of Oil Mines Regulations, 2017

Proper supervision been exercised to ensure that hot work of gas cutting been carried out at hazardous area in safe manner by competent person as per laid down procedures as required under provisions of Regulation 33(1) & (3) of Oil Mines Regulations, 2017.
hrec.statutes: Oil Mines Regulations 2017; OISD standard; SOP / code of practice / SMP
hrec.notes: Checked against narrative and Statement x.2 mineral/place counts.

hrec.ignition: Simultaneous blasting by this and adjoining mine in common boundary area
hrec.reported_cause: Blasts conducted simultaneously in a common boundary area by this and an adjoining granite mine; a rock piece flew about 113m and hit an outsider helping the surveyor.
hrec.cause_status: Official DGMS enquiry finding ("Had ... could have been averted")
hrec.situation: While a person was working (helping surveyor) in an opencast granite mine, suddenly blastings were conducted in common boundary area by blasters of the mine and adjoining granite mine simultaneously and a piece of rock, measuring about 22cm x14cm x 6cm, flew/projected to a distance of about 113m and hit him inflicting serious bodily injuries to which he succumbed while being taken to the hospital after 40 minutes.
findings: all persons within the danger zone been taken proper shelter before firing of shots, as required under the provisions of Regulation 164(1-A)(a)&(b) of the Metalliferous Mines Regulations, 1961

SOP for conducting blasting operations in mines been framed and implemented thereby willfully or negligently omit to do anything necessary for the safety of persons employed in the mines as required under Reg 181 of Metalliferous Mines Regulation 1961 read with Recommendation No. 9.2 of 11th Conference on Safety in Mines.
hrec.statutes: Metalliferous Mines Regulations 1961; SOP / code of practice / SMP
hrec.notes: Victim was an outsider.

hrec.ignition: Not reported (explosives detonated prematurely while being unloaded)
hrec.reported_cause: While eight persons unloaded explosives & detonators (quantity not known) from a car dickey under an unqualified supervisor, the explosives detonated prematurely, killing all eight, the supervisor and the driver.
hrec.cause_status: Official DGMS enquiry finding ("Had ... could have been averted")
hrec.situation: While eight persons were unloading explosives & detonators (quantity not known) from the dickey of a car which was being supervised by another person (unqualified supervisor), suddenly explosives detonated pre-maturely causing fatal inuries to all eight persons, the supervisor and the car driver (present at the site).
findings: the explosive(s), issued from the magazine, been taken into the mine in a heavily galvanized case or container of substantial construction and securely locked and the detonators been carried in a separate container constructed of non- conductive material and the explosives & detonators been carried separately as required under Regulation 157(1) & 157(2) of Metalliferous Mines Regualations, 1961

the duly qualified manager been appointed for overall management, control, supervision and direction of the mine as required under Section 17 of the Mines Act, 1952 read with Regulation 34(1) of the Metalliferous Mines Regulations, 1961

Asst. Manager, Mine Forman, Mining Mate & Blaster were appointed for supervision of the mining operations including blasting in the mine as required under Regulation 35, 37, 39 & 116 of the Metalliferous Mines Regulations, 1961

the persons been imparted basic training and undergone a course of training of handling & use of explosive as detailed in the 6th schedule as required under Rule 6 and 13(1) of the Mines Vocational Training Rule, 1966

hrec.reported_cause: Charged holes at a nearby site connected with detonating fuse and electric detonator exploded due to lightning; fly rock killed the mining mate deployed as blaster.
hrec.cause_status: Official DGMS enquiry finding ("Had ... could have been averted")
hrec.situation: While a mining mate deployed as blaster along with blasting Mazdoor and contractor was returning from one of the blasting site after disconnecting electric detonator from detonating fuse due to approach and progress of an electric storm, suddenly charged holes at other nearby site connected with detonating fuse and electric detonator exploded due to strike of lighting causing serious bodily injuries to mining mate due to fly rock to which he succumbed on the way to hospital while other escaped with minor injuries.
findings: the blaster himself taken adequate shelter along with his assistant during the approach and progress of an electric storm, as required under Regulation 164(1) of the Metalliferous Mines Regulations, 1961 read with DGMS Circular no.Tech.1/1995 and, the exposed detonating fuse been disconnected from already connected electric detonator at all the blasting site, coiled up and covered by something other than a metal plate so as to prevent the charged holes exploding prematurely by a local strike of the lighting, thus not negligently endangering life of the persons employed in the mine as required under Regulation 181 of the Metalliferous Mines Regulations, 1961 read with DGMS Circular no.Tech.01/1995.

a duly qualified blaster been appointed for preparation of charges, charging and stemming of holes by him or under his personnel supervision and firing shots by himself as required under Regulation 39 read with Regulation 160 of the Metalliferous Mines Regulations, 1961

sufficient warning, by efficient signals given over the entire area falling within a radius of 300 meters from the place of blasting and also ensured that all the persons within such area have taken proper shelter, before firing the shots as required under Regulation 164 (1-A) (b) of the Metalliferous Mines Regulations, 1961

guidance.measure: Dilute firedamp with adequate ventilation and sample the mine air for methane frequently, at many points.

refs.section: 2.1.6.1 Measures against accumulation of dangerous firedamp mixtures
refs.note: Calls adequate ventilation that dilutes firedamp the most effective way of preventing firedamp explosions, and frequent sampling of mine air for methane at several points an important preventive measure.
Tunlan mine (China, 2009, 78 deaths): very low air velocity in a crosscut let gas reach the flammable limit before it was ignited. The ventilation measure is derived from this case.

links: the working places including the unused working temporarily stopped been inspected and examined for ventilation and presence of inflammable gases within two hours before commencement of work in a shift and at least in every four hours during which shift continues, as required under Regulation 113(3)(b) of the Coal Mines Regulation 1957

guidance.measure: Keep development headings ventilated up to the face: auxiliary fans properly installed and maintained so air reaches within about 5 m of the face without recirculation, and the primary current used during idle shifts.
guidance.dgms_pattern: ventilation connection|coursing of current of air

refs.note: Auxiliary fans should be properly installed, maintained and located so that air is delivered within 5 m of the face and recirculation is eliminated; during weekends and idle shifts the place should be ventilated by the primary air current.

links: the galleries not been extended beyond 4.5m from the nearest ventilation connection without coursing of current of air up to a point within 4.5m of the face by means of a fire resistant pipes, tubes, brattices or any other material so as to ensure that the velocity of air current within 4.5m of the discontinued face is not less than 30m per minute to produce ventilation adequate to dilute gases that are inflammable or noxious so as to render them harmless, as required under the provisions of the Regulations 130(1), 146 (1) and Regulation 136A of the Coal Mines Regulation 1957

guidance.measure: In gassy caving panels, control goaf firedamp by methane drainage (in-mine or surface boreholes) or bleeder systems where ventilation alone cannot keep methane down.

refs.section: 2.1.6.1 (x) and 2.1.6.3 Control of firedamp emission / methane drainage
refs.note: Goaf firedamp in very gassy caving panels must be controlled by local or central drainage or surface boreholes; bleeder systems can move firedamp-air mixtures from caved areas to returns. Drainage is advised where ventilation alone cannot control methane.
Upper Big Branch (USA, 2010, 29 deaths): methane accumulated in the gob behind the shields migrated to the longwall face and tailgate before ignition.

guidance.measure: Inspect every ventilated working place each shift for methane (faces, blind ends, cavities, roof high places) with an approved detector, test before intentional roof falls, and keep records.

refs.note: Inspections should be carried out during every shift in every ventilated district for methane in the general body of air and at faces, blind ends, faults and roof cavities, using an approved methane detector; methane should be checked before an intentional roof fall; records should be kept.

guidance.measure: Keep smoking articles, matches and any other flame- or spark-producing devices out of the workings and explosive areas, and search persons for contraband.
guidance.dgms_pattern: capable of producing light, flame or spark|mobile telephone

refs.section: 2.1.6.2 (i) Measures against ignition of flammable firedamp mixtures
refs.note: All persons should be prohibited from carrying smoking articles, matches or other spark- or flame-making devices into the workings, and everyone entering the mine should be searched for contraband.

refs.section: 1.2 Recognition of Mine Gas Explosions Hazard
refs.note: Lists strict control of ignition sources and prohibition of smoking among the precautions against methane ignitions.

guidance.measure: Use only certified flameproof and intrinsically safe electrical apparatus, properly installed and maintained; cut power to districts where it is not needed and test for methane before re-energising.

refs.note: Only certified flame-proof and intrinsically-safe apparatus should be used in coal mines, properly installed, protected, operated and maintained; power should be cut off where equipment is not needed and methane tested immediately before it is energised.

Sparking from misuse or damage of electrical equipment can ignite methane gathered in poorly ventilated chambers; at Tunlan a poor-quality switch made the explosion-proof case fail and sparks escaped.

refs.section: 2.1.5 Causes of firedamp explosions: electric sparks
refs.note: Sparks from switchgear, damaged cables, signalling apparatus and faulty equipment are listed as ignition sources; minimum ignition energy is as low as 0.28 mJ near 8.3% methane.

mechanisms: Electrical or Mechanical Ignition of Explosive Atmosphere
guidance.measure: Fit methane monitors that automatically cut power to face machines and electrical equipment at the prescribed limit, and keep them maintained and checked.

refs.note: A reliable methane monitor or cut-out that automatically cuts off power at the prescribed concentration may be installed; methane monitors should be fitted on face-cutting, continuous-mining, longwall and loading equipment and checked at regular intervals.

mechanisms: Electrical or Mechanical Ignition of Explosive Atmosphere
guidance.measure: When the main fan stops, cut power in return airways; if an auxiliary fan stops, stop electrical equipment there until ventilation is restored; make ventilation changes only when the mine is idle and power is off.

refs.note: States these three power-and-ventilation rules.

mechanisms: Electrical or Mechanical Ignition of Explosive Atmosphere
guidance.measure: Protect and suspend trailing cables, earth ventilation ducting and machinery, and use antistatic sheeting, hoses and belts to prevent static sparks.

refs.note: Vulnerable trailing cables should be suspended and protected; ventilation ducting should be earthed and only antistatic polythene sheeting, hoses and belts used.
Static from belts and dust-laden ducting can produce sparks; earthing all machinery to discharge static greatly reduces the danger.

mechanisms: Electrical or Mechanical Ignition of Explosive Atmosphere
guidance.measure: Control frictional ignition at cutting and drilling machines: sharp, suitable picks, water sprays at the picks, adequate ventilation of the cut, and no light-alloy materials.

refs.note: Frictional sparks from metal-to-rock contact during cutting and drilling (especially in siliceous bands or pyrite) are a major ignition source; precautions include sharp picks, water sprays directed at the picks, lower pick speed, ventilating the cut, and prohibiting light alloys.
At Upper Big Branch the shearer cutting into sandstone roof produced the sparks that ignited methane.

guidance.measure: Where firedamp may be present, keep blasting to a minimum, examine for methane immediately before charging and firing, and use water stemming or permitted blasting alternatives.

refs.note: Blasting with explosives should be restricted to a minimum, an examination for methane should be made immediately before blasting, and water stemming or alternatives to ordinary explosives may be used.
Blasting in coal and in roadhead rippings and drifts was a dangerous source of firedamp ignition in the past.

Welding, cutting and soldering should be performed only by competent persons under constant supervision of a qualified person, at places free from danger due to firedamp or coal dust, with fire-extinguishing appliances and stone dust immediately available.

guidance.measure: Stone-dust (rock-dust) all roadways so that mine dust always holds at least the prescribed incombustible content, raised where methane is present, and re-apply it at regular intervals.

refs.note: Gives the minimum incombustible content of mine dust as 70% in India, 80% in Germany and 65% in the USA, to be raised for each 1% of methane in the air; stone dust must be applied at regular intervals because coal dust keeps depositing. Notes that stone dust is not recommended in base metal mines (p. 137).

Rock dust acts as isolator and heat sink; MSHA raised the US requirement in 2010 to at least 80% total incombustible content plus 0.4% for each 0.1% methane; rock dust should contain at most 5% combustible matter and 4% silica.

guidance.conflict: The books give different US figures (Ramlu 65%; Cheng 80% after MSHA's 2010 rule). Ramlu's 70% is the figure for India. Both are kept as written.

guidance.measure: Reduce the formation and spread of coal dust: water infusion of the seam, wet cutting with sprays, hooded and water-sprayed conveyor transfer points, preventing spillage, and regular cleaning of deposited dust from roadways.

refs.section: 2.2.9.1 Measures which prevent or reduce formation and dissemination of coal dust
refs.note: Lists water infusion, wet cutting and sprays, covering conveyors and enclosing and spraying transfer points, avoiding spillage, dust collectors, and systematic cleaning of haulage roads and returns.

guidance.measure: Before shotfiring in coal, neutralise or consolidate dust within 10–20 m of the face with water or inert dust.

refs.section: 2.2.9.2 Measures against ignition of dust accumulations
refs.note: Dust at working coal faces within a radius of 10 to 20 m should be neutralised or consolidated with water or inert dust before shotfiring.
Water sprays installed not more than 20 m from working faces are regarded as effective against initiation of coal-dust and firedamp explosions by blasting.

guidance.measure: Confine explosions with correctly sited, designed, installed and maintained stone-dust or water barriers or explosion stoppings.

refs.note: Lists generalized wetting, stonedusting, stonedust barriers, explosion stoppings, salt zones, water barriers and triggered barriers as measures to confine a coal-dust explosion.

refs.section: 2.3.1 Rock Dusting; 2.3.2 Stonedust and Water Barriers
refs.note: Barrier failures are mostly due to improper location, design, installation and maintenance; barriers placed closer than 60 m to the ignition point may not be dispersed. Cheng adds that the effectiveness of water barriers is now questioned.

guidance.conflict: Ramlu lists water barriers among confinement measures; Cheng reports their effectiveness is questioned after Chinese experience. Both views are shown.

guidance.measure: Consider water-mist curtains at working faces and active explosion-suppression systems, and combine two or more control methods rather than relying on one.

refs.note: Water mist significantly suppresses methane-air explosions and suits working-face areas; active suppression systems detect the flame and release agent to stop propagation; Cheng recommends using two or more methods together.

mechanisms: Spontaneous Heating, Fire and Explosion Escalation
guidance.measure: Seal or ventilate worked-out areas promptly, using solid, substantial and incombustible seals sited where strata convergence is low, built to correct procedures and designed to withstand explosion pressure.

refs.note: Abandoned areas must be ventilated or sealed; the 1969 US Coal Act required solid, substantial and incombustible seals; seals should be located where entry closure or crushing is minimal, and high-quality construction reduces leakage.

Darby Mine No. 1 (2006, 5 deaths): improper seal construction and unsafe repair work led to an explosion behind seals; seals rated 140 kPa failed in US incidents, where 345–500 kPa standards abroad did not.

refs.note: Worked-out areas should be effectively sealed off as soon as possible or ventilated, with bleeder entries if ventilated.

mechanisms: Spontaneous Heating, Fire and Explosion Escalation
guidance.measure: Monitor sealed-area atmospheres for explosibility, especially in the critical period after sealing, and make an explosive atmosphere safe by inert-gas injection or controlled fresh-air dilution; do not open or rebuild seals without assessment.

refs.note: A newly sealed atmosphere passes through the explosive range (methane 5–15%) during a 'critical' period when most sealed-area explosions have occurred.

refs.note: To make an explosive sealed atmosphere safe, move it out of the explosive triangle by injecting inert gas or ventilating with fresh air; adding combustible gas is too dangerous.

guidance.measure: Prevent spontaneous heating: independent panel ventilation, extraction within the incubation period, minimal air leakage, removal of loose coal and combustible waste, daily CO checks in district returns, and inspections every shift and on idle days.

refs.note: Lists development, coal-winning, roof-control, ventilation and inspection measures, including panels with independent ventilation, complete extraction within the incubation period, clearing loose coal and combustible waste, checking return air for CO at least once a day, and inspection each shift and on idle days.

mechanisms: Spontaneous Heating, Fire and Explosion Escalation
guidance.measure: When sealing a fire where a firegas or firedamp explosion is possible, first erect high-strength, explosion-proof temporary stoppings in intake and return, sited well away from the fire seat, then the permanent stoppings.

refs.note: High-strength explosion-proof, airtight temporary stoppings should first be erected in intake and return airways, followed later by permanent stoppings, with stoppings sited as far from the fire seat as possible.

mechanisms: Metal Mine: Gas, Dust and Other Explosion Mechanisms
guidance.measure: In sulphide-ore (base metal) mines, reduce ore-dust explosion risk during blasting: low-incendivity explosives, a drill pattern that prevents rifling, accurate drilling, careful charge loading, inert stemming in hole collars, washing down walls and backs before blasting, and water-mist curtains during the blast.

refs.note: Sulphide ore-dust explosions occurred during blasting in Canadian base metal mines with pyrite/pyrrhotite ores; lists these seven precautionary measures.

guidance.measure: Limit the spread of an explosion: separate ventilation districts with robust air-crossings, explosion-proof blasting dams in long gassy headings, measures against coal-dust propagation, and an efficient rescue organisation.

refs.note: Lists these four ways of localizing firedamp explosions.
